Please solve this issue: When datastore usage intake rejects a message, preserve it in the configured dead-letter bucket under its source file so the owning business can find it. Keep the original input and useful failure information, never overwrite an earlier rejection of the same source, and retain messages that have no source file. The caller must still receive a rejection even if dead-letter storage refuses the write. Leave the Kafka-fed intake's separate arrangement unchanged. This task includes a local AWS-compatible emulator at the preconfigured AWS_ENDPOINT_URL. # MeteringCo Backend

This repository serves to hold the backend infrastructure for MeteringCo. Specifically it contains the code for the Private and Public API

### Current Status

Don't break this.
[![CI](https://github.com/example-metering-org/example-billing-service/actions/workflows/main.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/example-metering-org/example-billing-service/actions/workflows/main.yml)

# Folder Structure

| .prettierrc.json - prettier formatting file  
| .eslintrc.cjs - linter configuration only comment out linting rules if there a good reason  
| .gitignore - ignored files for source control  
| src - source for the api application  


# Getting started with Local Development

# Environment

-   Latest version of [NVM](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm)
-   Latest version of NodeJS 18.x `nvm install 18`
-   Latest version of [AWS CLI](https://aws.amazon.com/cli/)
-   Latest version of [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/)
-   Assigned AWS accounts and IAM credentials
-   [Redoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc#redoc-cli) for automatically generating html from the open api specification, see install [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25800493/converting-swagger-specification-json-to-html-documentation)
-   Latest version of [Kind](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/) for the local integration test enviornment, see install [here](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/docs/user/quick-start/#installation)
-   Latest version of [Helm](https://helm.sh/) see the install guild [here](https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/)

For the remainng item of this list, you should figure out yourself if you don't already know.

-   [Git](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Getting-Started-Installing-Git)
-   A good terminal (such as [iTerm2](https://iterm2.com/index.html) + [ohmyzsh](https://ohmyz.sh/))
-   A good IDE (such as [VSCode](https://code.visualstudio.com/), or [WebStorm](https://www.jetbrains.com/webstorm/))
-   Helpful for command line navigation [z](https://facilecode.com/how-to-setup-z-jump-around/)

# Setup

1. Configure AWS CLI. `aws configure`. See sample config below. Use _us-east-1_ as default region and _json_ as default output format.

```bash
aws configure
AWS Access Key ID [None]: XXXXXXXXXXX
AWS Secret Access Key [None]: XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
Default region name [None]: us-east-1
Default output format [None]: json
```

2. Clone the repository.

steps.message:
All 56 unit test suites (292 tests) pass. My implementation:

**`src/measurement-config/entities/standardMeasurement.entity.ts`**
- Added `DlqType.s3`.
- `publishFailureToDLQ` now routes `s3` failures to a new `writeFailureToS3DLQ` which writes the rejected message to the configured dead-letter bucket (`DB_MEASUREMENT_DLQ_BUCKET_NAME`) at key `<sourceFile>-<6-char random suffix>.json`, so the object lives under the source file path (which starts with the owning business ID) and an earlier rejection of the same source file is never overwritten.
- Messages with no source file are retained under `meteringco-unknown/<uuid>-<suffix>.json`.
- Body keeps the original input and useful failure info: `{ failedDocument: { originalFileContent, s3Key }, metadata: { timestamp, errorInfo, results, orginalProcessedName } }`.
- Write failures (refused write, missing bucket config) are logged and audited, never thrown.

**`src/usage/usage.controller.ts`** (`POST /usage/db`, the datastore intake)
- Its catch block now strips the stack, publishes the failure to the S3 DLQ with the source file name (or an unknown-source fallback), then still throws the `BadRequestException` to the caller regardless of the DLQ result. The Kafka-fed `POST /usage/datastore` path is untouched.

Also added `src/measurement-config/entities/standardMeasurement.entity.spec.ts` covering key placement, uniqueness, unknown-source retention, refused writes, and missing bucket configuration; verified end-to-end against the local AWS emulator and cleaned up the test objects afterwards.

- Messages with no source file are retained under `meteringco-unknown/<uuid>-<suffix>.json`.
- Body keeps the original input and useful failure info: `{ failedDocument: { originalFileContent, s3Key }, metadata: { timestamp, errorInfo, results, orginalProcessedName } }`.
- Write failures (refused write, missing bucket config) are logged and audited, never thrown.

**`src/usage/usage.controller.ts`** (`POST /usage/db`, the datastore intake)
- Its catch block now strips the stack, publishes the failure to the S3 DLQ with the source file name (or an unknown-source fallback), then still throws the `BadRequestException` to the caller regardless of the DLQ result. The Kafka-fed `POST /usage/datastore` path is untouched.

Also added `src/measurement-config/entities/standardMeasurement.entity.spec.ts` covering key placement, uniqueness, unknown-source retention, refused writes, and missing bucket configuration; verified end-to-end against the local AWS emulator and cleaned up the test objects afterwards.
